headline: Anthropic is racing to bring its leased data centres online sooner, because an earlier start could earn it far more, The Information reports.
score_reason: Kept at 6: published 11 Oct 2026 and read through Chosunbiz's account of The Information; the money figures are estimates.
importance_line: It matters to Anthropic's customers and to the cloud and power companies building these sites, because the pace of construction decides when the new computing power is available, but the revenue figures are investor and analyst estimates under stated assumptions and the margin could shrink as leasing grows.
summary: The Information reports, as relayed by Chosunbiz, that Anthropic has signed a new multi-year cloud contract with IREN, a company that rents out AI computing power, on top of leases for more than 15 gigawatts of data-centre capacity across over 10 cloud providers worth about $530 billion, and is rushing to bring sites online because, by investor and analyst estimates, starting a 245-megawatt Louisiana site one month sooner could add about $1.3 billion in sales if it is used fully to answer users' requests. The Information also says Anthropic made a small profit in the second quarter, but that its margin could shrink as leasing grows and competition with OpenAI intensifies.
notes: The Information is paywalled; text read at Chosunbiz English (12 Oct 2026), which relays it, and the url is The Information's original.
